To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the bandgap of semiconducting nanotubes shrinks as the doping level increases and the dielectric environment is changed.

(1) the bandgap of individual semiconducting single-wall carbon nanotubes (SWCNTs) shrinks by up to 1.0 eV as the doping density increases from p-type (holes) to n-type (electrons), and (2) the bandgap shrinks further by up to 0.4 eV when the nanotube is placed in contact with a dielectric (SiO2).
the bandgap of semiconducting nanotubes decreases with increasing doping and decreasing dielectric screening, as a result of strong electron-phonon interactions.
